 This Land Acquisition Appeal Having Been Finally
 Heard On 12.03.2025, The Court On The Same Day Delivered
 The Following:
Judgment
Easwaran S., J.
The appeal arises out of the judgment and decree dated 18.12.2020 in L.A.R.No.201 of 2007 on the files of the Sub Court, Muvattupuzha.

2. The brief facts for disposal of the appeal are as follows:
An extent of 0.98 Ares of land in Sy.No.30/4-8 of Muvattupuzha Village was acquired for the purpose of upgradation of Muvattupuzha - Thodupuzha Road by K.S.T.P.
The Land Acquisition Officer fixed the land value at Rs.29,522/- per Are.

Section 4(1)
notification was issued on 10.12.2002, and the land was taken possession on 21.02.2005.

Dissatisfied with the amount awarded by the Land Acquisition Officer,
the claimant filed an application for reference under Section 18 of the erstwhile Land Acquisition Act.
The grievance of the claimant was that the Land Acquisition Officer did not fix the correct value for the improvements and also for the demolition of the compound wall.

Though the notification was issued on 10.12.2002, on 11.11.2006, it is alleged that the respondents, along with the contractors, demolished the newly built compound wall and forcefully took the possession of L.A.A.No.136/21 :: 3 ::
2025:KER:20963 5 cents of property destroying the valuable improvements.
3. In support of the claim for enhancement of the value of the improvements, the claimant produced Ext.A8, a report of the expert, and examined AW4.
In addition to the above, the claimant also took out Advocate Commission for local inspection, who submitted Ext.A3 report.
The Advocate Commissioner was also examined as AW2.
The Reference Court, relying upon Ext.A3 report, by judgment and decree dated 31.08.2011, awarded a total compensation of Rs.45,49,000/- for the structures and improvements.
Aggrieved by the judgment, the State preferred L.A.App.No.378 of 2012 before this Court.

By judgment dated 26.09.2018, the Single Bench of this Court allowed the appeal, setting aside the judgment and decree dated 31.08.2011 in L.A.R.No.201 of 2007, and remanded the matter back for fresh consideration to the Reference Court.
The Reference Court was directed to re-fix the value of improvements and compensation for the structures, allowing the parties to adduce fresh evidence.
On remand, the claimant did not adduce any evidence but relied on the existing evidence before the Reference Court.

The Reference Court, on appreciation of the Mathew vs State Of Kerla on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198009196/
2 evidence, found that the determination of the land value by the Land Acquisition Officer was more beneficial to the claimant than adopting a capitalisation method and therefore answered the reference accordingly.

Aggrieved by the judgment now rendered L.A.A.No.136/21 :: 4 ::
2025:KER:20963 pursuant to the remand, the appellant has preferred the present appeal.
3. Heard Smt.N.Sudha, the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant/claimant and Sri.T.K.Shajahan, the learned senior Government Pleader appearing on behalf of the State.

4. The learned counsel for the appellant placed extensive reliance on the report of the expert, who had valued the improvements as well as the compensation towards the demolition of the retaining wall, which was marked as Ext.A8 before the Reference Court.

According to the learned counsel, the oral testimony of AW4, coupled with Ext.A8 and Ext.A3 report of the Advocate Commissioner, establishes the claim for enhancement of compensation towards the value of improvements.

5. On the other hand, the learned senior Government Pleader appearing on behalf of the State pointed out that this Court had remanded the matter back to the Reference Court by judgment dated 26.09.2018 in L.A.App.No.378 of 2012 in order to specifically enable the parties to adduce evidence to substantiate their contentions.

In the absence of any evidence on the side of the claimant after the remand, according to the learned senior Government Pleader, the findings of the Reference Court are not liable to be interfered with.
We have considered the rival submissions made across the bar, and are of the considered view that there is force in the submissions of the learned senior Government Pleader.

In L.A.App.No.378 of 2012, this Court specifically found that Ext.A8 and the evidence of AW4, if relied on, will result in a windfall of compensation to the claimant and therefore the compensation requires a re-determination.
For the said purpose, the parties were granted an opportunity to adduce evidence in support of their claim.

In as much as the claimant having failed to adduce any reliable supporting evidence to substantiate his claim under Ext.A8, we are of the view that the Reference Court cannot be found fault with for answering the reference in the manner which has been now done.

7. Faced with the above situation, the learned counsel for the appellant/claimant submits that Mathew vs State Of Kerla on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198009196/
3 though this Court has granted an opportunity for adducing evidence, non-availing of such opportunity by itself should not turn out to be detrimental to the interests of the claimant since the Reference Court was also duty bound to determine the compensation based on the available evidence.

sentences.text:
The learned counsel also further submitted that if this Court is of the view that the appellant/claimant ought to have adduced further evidence in support of his claim under Ext.A8, an opportunity be granted for the purpose of L.A.A.No.136/21 :: 6 ::
2025:KER:20963 adducing evidence so as to sustain his claim.
8. We find that the parties have been litigating over the claim for improvements from 2007 onwards.
Be that as it may, the endeavour of the Court should always be to determine the compensation towards the improvements which were destroyed by the State in pursuance of the purported acquisition.

Viewed in the above perspective, we are of the view that an opportunity can be extended to the appellant/claimant to substantiate the claim in Ext.A8 by producing supporting material that would justify the calculation of compensation mentioned in Ext.A8.
Therefore, we hereby set aside the judgment and decree dated 18.12.2020 in L.A.R.No.201 of 2007, and remand the matter for the limited purpose stated above.
For the purpose as stated above, the parties are directed to appear before the Reference Court on 10.04.2025.
On the appearance of the parties before the Reference Court, the Reference Court shall make every endeavour to dispose of the reference as expeditiously as possible in accordance with priority.

The appellant/claimant is entitled to the refund of the entire court fee paid on the appeal.
9.

We are also informed that pursuant to the judgment dated 18.12.2020 in answering the reference as above, the State has moved an application for restitution and also for recovery of the amount which L.A.A.No.136/21 :: 7 ::
2025:KER:20963 was withdrawn by the appellant pursuant to the interim order passed by this Court in L.A.App.No.378 of 2012.

Since we have set aside the judgment, answering the reference, and remanded the matter for fresh consideration,
we order that all steps for recovery of the amount withdrawn by the appellant shall be kept in abeyance till such time as the Reference Court re-considers the matter and renders a revised judgment as indicated above.
The appellant is also entitled to refund of court fee.
The L.A.A. is allowed by remand.
No order as to cost.

Sd/-
DR. A.K.JAYASANKARAN NAMBIAR JUDGE Sd/-
